```{r}
#TASK 1: 
##########################################################
# FECUNDITY DECAY FUNCTION
# Source: Rothman et al. (2013) - Table 3
# Volitional determinants and age-related decline in fecundability
##########################################################

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(officer)
library(flextable)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 1: Extract data from Rothman et al. Table 3 (Adjusted model)
#=============================================================================

# Data from Table 3 - Adjusted fecundability ratios (FR)
# Reference category: women aged 20-24 years (FR = 1.00)

rothman_data <- data.frame(
  age_cat = c("20-24", "25-29", "30-34", "35-40"),
  # Use midpoints for modeling
  age_mid = c(22, 27, 32, 37.5),  # 37.5 as midpoint of 35-40
  # Adjusted FR from Table 3
  FR = c(1.00, 1.03, 1.05, 0.77),
  # 95% CI from Table 3
  FR_low = c(1.00, 0.90, 0.89, 0.62),
  FR_high = c(1.00, 1.18, 1.23, 0.97),
  # Sample sizes from Table 2
  n_pregnancies = c(314, 996, 625, 140),
  n_total = c(466, 1355, 791, 208)
)

cat("=== Rothman et al. (2013) Fecundability Ratios ===\n")
print(rothman_data[, c("age_cat", "age_mid", "FR", "FR_low", "FR_high")])

#=============================================================================
# STEP 2: Set new baseline at age 25-29 (use age 27 as reference point)
#=============================================================================

# We want 25-29 age band to be the reference (FR = 1.00)
# Current: age 20-24 = 1.00, age 25-29 = 1.03
# Standardization factor = 1 / 1.03 = 0.9709

baseline_age <- 27  # Midpoint of 25-29
baseline_FR_original <- rothman_data$FR[rothman_data$age_cat == "25-29"]  # 1.03
standardization_factor <- 1 / baseline_FR_original

cat("\n=== Standardizing to Age 25-29 Baseline ===\n")
cat("Original FR at 25-29:", baseline_FR_original, "\n")
cat("Standardization factor:", round(standardization_factor, 4), "\n")
cat("(Multiply all FR by", round(standardization_factor, 4), ")\n")

# Create standardized dataset with age 25-29 as reference
rothman_std <- rothman_data
rothman_std$FR_std <- rothman_data$FR * standardization_factor
rothman_std$FR_low_std <- rothman_data$FR_low * standardization_factor
rothman_std$FR_high_std <- rothman_data$FR_high * standardization_factor

cat("\n=== Standardized FR (25-29 = 1.00) ===\n")
print(rothman_std[, c("age_cat", "age_mid", "FR_std", "FR_low_std", "FR_high_std")])

#=============================================================================
# STEP 3: Calculate decay rate from observed decline
#=============================================================================

# Use ages 27 (baseline) through 37.5 to calculate decay
# FR at age 27: 1.00 (standardized)
# FR at age 32: 1.05 * 0.9709 = 1.019
# FR at age 37.5: 0.77 * 0.9709 = 0.748

FR_27 <- rothman_std$FR_std[rothman_std$age_cat == "25-29"]  # 1.00
FR_32 <- rothman_std$FR_std[rothman_std$age_cat == "30-34"]  # ~1.019
FR_37.5 <- rothman_std$FR_std[rothman_std$age_cat == "35-40"]  # ~0.748

# Calculate decay rate using 27 → 37.5 (10.5 years)
decay_rate <- log(FR_37.5 / FR_27) / 10.5

cat("\n=== Decay Rate Calculation ===\n")
cat("FR at age 27 (baseline):", round(FR_27, 3), "\n")
cat("FR at age 32:", round(FR_32, 3), "\n")
cat("FR at age 37.5:", round(FR_37.5, 3), "\n")
cat("Annual decay rate:", round(decay_rate, 4), 
    "(", round(100 * (1 - exp(decay_rate)), 1), "% decline per year)\n")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 4: Derive empirical log-scale SE at each observed Rothman age point
#         and fit a linear model to predict SE across ages 25-50.
#
# Rationale: Rather than imposing an arbitrary uncertainty growth rate,
# we derive SE directly from Rothman et al.'s published 95% CIs at each
# observed age point (27, 32, 37.5), then fit a linear regression of
# SE ~ age through those points. This gives a fully data-driven,
# auditable SE curve grounded in the source publication.
#
# Note: The 20-24 reference category is excluded — its CI is degenerate
# (FR fixed at 1.00 with SE = 0 by construction, not by data).
#=============================================================================

# Convert to log scale
rothman_std$logFR     <- log(rothman_std$FR_std)
rothman_std$logFR_low <- log(rothman_std$FR_low_std)
rothman_std$logFR_high<- log(rothman_std$FR_high_std)
rothman_std$logFR_se  <- (rothman_std$logFR_high - rothman_std$logFR_low) / (2 * 1.96)

# Exclude reference category (SE = 0 by construction, not informative)
se_fit_data <- rothman_std[rothman_std$age_cat != "20-24",
                            c("age_mid", "logFR_se")]

cat("\n=== Empirical log-scale SEs from Rothman CIs ===\n")
print(se_fit_data, row.names = FALSE)

# Fit linear regression: SE ~ age
se_lm <- lm(logFR_se ~ age_mid, data = se_fit_data)

cat("\n=== Linear SE model (SE ~ age) ===\n")
print(summary(se_lm))
cat("Intercept:", round(coef(se_lm)[1], 6), "\n")
cat("Slope (SE per year of age):", round(coef(se_lm)[2], 6), "\n")

# Baseline SE at age 27 from the fitted model
se_baseline <- predict(se_lm, newdata = data.frame(age_mid = 27))
cat("\nFitted SE at age 27:", round(se_baseline, 4),
    "(vs raw:", round(rothman_std$logFR_se[rothman_std$age_cat == "25-29"], 4), ")\n")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 5: Generate predictions for ages 25-50
#=============================================================================

age_seq <- 25:50
pred_dat <- data.frame(
  age = age_seq,
  years_since_baseline = age_seq - 27
)

# Exponential decay formula for log-mean
pred_dat$logFR_mean <- log(FR_27) + decay_rate * pred_dat$years_since_baseline

# Data-driven SE: predicted from linear model fitted to Rothman CIs.
# SE is constrained to be non-negative (extrapolation below age 27
# could theoretically give negative fitted values; pmax guards against this).
pred_dat$logFR_se <- pmax(
  predict(se_lm, newdata = data.frame(age_mid = pred_dat$age)),
  1e-6   # floor: SE cannot be zero or negative
)

cat("\n=== Fitted SE at key ages (data-driven, from Rothman CIs) ===\n")
key_check <- pred_dat[pred_dat$age %in% c(25, 27, 30, 32, 35, 37, 40, 45, 50),
                       c("age", "logFR_se")]
print(key_check, row.names = FALSE)

# Convert to original scale with log-normal properties
pred_dat$FR_mean <- exp(pred_dat$logFR_mean + 0.5 * pred_dat$logFR_se^2)

# 95% CI on original scale
pred_dat$FR_low  <- exp(pred_dat$logFR_mean - 1.96 * pred_dat$logFR_se)
pred_dat$FR_high <- exp(pred_dat$logFR_mean + 1.96 * pred_dat$logFR_se)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 6: Display key results
#=============================================================================

cat("\n=== Exponential Decay Model Results (Baseline Age 27) ===\n")
cat("Annual decay rate:", round(decay_rate, 4), 
    paste0("(", round(100 * (1 - exp(decay_rate)), 1), "%/year)\n"))

key_ages <- c(27, 30, 32, 35, 37, 40, 45, 50)
cat("\nKey age points:\n")
print(pred_dat[pred_dat$age %in% key_ages, 
               c("age", "FR_mean", "FR_low", "FR_high")], 
      row.names = FALSE)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 7: Create Markov model age bands (for 25-50 population)
#=============================================================================

pred_dat$age_band <- cut(
  pred_dat$age,
  breaks = c(25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 51),  # 51 to include age 50
  right = FALSE,
  labels = c("25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-50")
)

# Aggregate by evaluating parameters at each band midpoint age.
# This ensures:
#   (a) logFR_mean for 25-29 = exactly 0.000 (midpoint 27 = anchor)
#   (b) logFR_mean for 45-50 matches PSA parameter at age 47

band_midpoints <- c("25-29" = 27, "30-34" = 32, "35-39" = 37,
                    "40-44" = 42, "45-50" = 47)

band_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(band_midpoints), function(band) {
  mid  <- band_midpoints[band]
  row  <- pred_dat[pred_dat$age == mid, ]
  lmu  <- row$logFR_mean
  lvar <- row$logFR_se^2
  data.frame(
    age_band     = band,
    n_ages       = sum(pred_dat$age_band == band),
    midpoint_age = mid,
    logFR_mean   = lmu,
    logFR_var    = lvar,
    FR_mean      = exp(lmu + 0.5 * lvar),
    FR_sd        = sqrt((exp(lvar) - 1) * exp(2 * lmu + lvar)),
    FR_low       = exp(lmu - 1.96 * sqrt(lvar)),
    FR_high      = exp(lmu + 1.96 * sqrt(lvar)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
band_summary$age_band <- factor(band_summary$age_band,
                                 levels = names(band_midpoints))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Force FR_mean = 1.000 exactly for the 25-29 reference band.
#
# Why: PSA draws use exp(NORM.INV(RAND(), mu, sigma)), so the mean of those
# draws = exp(mu + 0.5*sigma^2). For the deterministic base case (FR_mean)
# to equal the mean of the PSA draws we need:
#   exp(mu + 0.5*sigma^2) = 1  =>  mu = -0.5*sigma^2
#
# The decay curve anchors at age 27 giving log_mu = 0, but
# exp(0 + 0.5*s^2) = 1.0024 != 1. Back-calculating mu closes this exactly.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
band_summary$logFR_mean[1] <- -0.5 * band_summary$logFR_var[1]
band_summary$FR_mean[1]    <- exp(band_summary$logFR_mean[1] +
                                   0.5 * band_summary$logFR_var[1])  # = 1.000 exactly
band_summary$FR_low[1]     <- exp(band_summary$logFR_mean[1] -
                                   1.96 * sqrt(band_summary$logFR_var[1]))
band_summary$FR_high[1]    <- exp(band_summary$logFR_mean[1] +
                                   1.96 * sqrt(band_summary$logFR_var[1]))

cat("\n=== Markov Model Age Bands (25-50 population) ===\n")
print(band_summary[, c("age_band", "midpoint_age", "FR_mean", "FR_low", "FR_high")],
      row.names = FALSE)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 8: Standardize so 25-29 = 1.00 (for Table in manuscript)
#=============================================================================
# FR_mean for 25-29 is now exactly 1.000 by construction above,

standardization_factor_bands <- 1 / band_summary$FR_mean[1]   # = 1.000 exactly

standardized_bands <- band_summary
standardized_bands$FR_mean <- band_summary$FR_mean * standardization_factor_bands
standardized_bands$FR_low  <- band_summary$FR_low  * standardization_factor_bands
standardized_bands$FR_high <- band_summary$FR_high * standardization_factor_bands

cat("\n=== Standardized FR (25-29 = 1.00) for Manuscript Table ===\n")
cat("Standardization factor:", round(standardization_factor_bands, 6),
    "(should be exactly 1)\n\n")

table_output <- standardized_bands[, c("age_band", "midpoint_age", "FR_mean", "FR_low", "FR_high")]
table_output$FR_mean <- round(table_output$FR_mean, 3)
table_output$FR_low <- round(table_output$FR_low, 3)
table_output$FR_high <- round(table_output$FR_high, 3)

print(table_output, row.names = FALSE)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 9: PSA Parameters (log-normal distributions)
#=============================================================================

psa_params <- pred_dat[pred_dat$age %in% c(27, 32, 37, 42, 47), 
                       c("age", "logFR_mean", "logFR_se")]
psa_params$distribution <- "lognormal"
psa_params$mu <- psa_params$logFR_mean
psa_params$sigma <- psa_params$logFR_se

cat("\n=== PSA Parameters (for log-normal distribution) ===\n")
print(psa_params[, c("age", "mu", "sigma")], row.names = FALSE)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 10: Plot results
#=============================================================================

plot(pred_dat$age, pred_dat$FR_mean, type = "l", lwd = 2,
     ylim = c(0, max(pred_dat$FR_high, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1),
     xlab = "Age", ylab = "Fecundability Ratio (FR)",
     main = paste("Fecundability Decline with Age\n",
                  "(Baseline: Age 27 = 1.00)"))

# Add confidence interval
polygon(c(pred_dat$age, rev(pred_dat$age)),
        c(pred_dat$FR_low, rev(pred_dat$FR_high)),
        col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border = NA)

# Add Rothman data points (standardized)
points(rothman_std$age_mid, rothman_std$FR_std, 
       col = "red", pch = 16, cex = 1.5)

# Add reference lines
abline(v = 27, lty = 2, col = "gray")
abline(h = 1, lty = 3, col = "gray")
abline(v = c(30, 35, 40, 45, 50), lty = 3, col = "lightgray")

legend("topright", 
       legend = c("Exponential decay", "Rothman data (standardized)", 
                  "95% CI", "Baseline age 27"),
       col = c("black", "red", rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), "gray"),
       lty = c(1, NA, 1, 2), lwd = c(2, NA, 10, 1),
       pch = c(NA, 16, 15, NA),
       bg = "white")

print(band_summary)


# Note on log-scale mu:

# standardization_factor_bands corrects only the *original-scale* FR_mean for the Jensen's inequality term (0.5 * sigma^2); it must NOT be added on the log scale,or it would shift mu away from 0 for the reference band.

appendix_table <- data.frame(
  Age_group    = as.character(standardized_bands$age_band),
  FR_mean      = round(standardized_bands$FR_mean, 3),
  FR_SD        = round(band_summary$FR_sd * standardization_factor_bands, 3),
  Distribution = "Log-normal",
  Log_mu       = round(band_summary$logFR_mean, 3),
  Log_sigma    = round(sqrt(band_summary$logFR_var), 3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Create formatted appendix table
ft_appendix <- flextable(appendix_table) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    Age_group    = "Age group",
    FR_mean      = "FR mean",
    FR_SD        = "FR SD",
    Distribution = "Distribution",
    Log_mu       = "Log-scale mu",
    Log_sigma    = "Log-scale sigma"
  ) %>%
  set_caption(caption = "Supplementary Table S1. Fecundity ratio parameters for probabilistic sensitivity analysis") %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  autofit()

# Save as Word documents
save_as_docx(ft_appendix, 
             path = "Appendix_Table_Fecundity_PSA.docx")
```

```{r}
#TASK 2: IMPUTATION FOR UP OUTCOME PROBABILITIES, ALPHA AND BETA.
# UP Outcome conditional probabilities. Here, we do not have proportions of UP outcomes for age 45-49, but we do have from age 25-44. I will use PMM to find the values for age 45-49 and thereafter calculate conditional probabilities for each UP outcome (live birth, Abortion, Miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy) i.e the probability of each outcome conditional upon transition into the UP state. 

#source: 
#Cost of unintended pregnancy in Norway: a role for long-acting reversible contraception by Henry et al
#Detecting and Dating Early Non‐live Pregnancy Outcomes: Generation of a Novel Pregnancy Algorithm From Norwegian Linked Health Registries DOI: 10.1002/pds.70002 

library(dplyr)
library(mice)      # For multiple imputation
library(MCMCpack)  # For rdirichlet function

# STEP 1: Source data with updated age groups (starting at 25)
#=============================================================================

henry_data <- data.frame(
  age_group = c("25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-50"),
  age_midpoint = c(27, 32.5, 37.5, 42.5, 47.5),
  live_birth = c(0.25, 0.30, 0.45, 0.50, NA),  # 25-29 assumed 0.25 based on Henry Table 1 (20-24:0.45, 25-29:0.25)
  abortion = c(0.96, 0.96, 0.98, 0.98, NA)     # 25-29 assumed 0.96 based on Henry Table 1
)

print(henry_data)

#===========================================================================
# STEP 2: Impute missing values for age 45-49 using PMM
#===========================================================================

set.seed(123)  # For reproducible results

# Create a copy for imputation
impute_data <- henry_data[, c("age_midpoint", "live_birth", "abortion")]

# Run multiple imputation for age 45-50
cat("\nRunning multiple imputation for age 45-50...\n")
imp <- mice(impute_data, 
            m = 5,           # Create 5 imputed datasets
            maxit = 10,      # Run 10 iterations
            method = "pmm",  # Predictive Mean Matching
            print = FALSE)   # Suppress output

# Extract and pool the imputed values
imputed_sets <- complete(imp, "long")

# Filter for age 45-49 and calculate averages
age_45_imputed <- imputed_sets %>%
  filter(age_midpoint == 47.5) %>%
  group_by(.imp) %>%
  summarise(
    live_birth_imp = mean(live_birth),
    abortion_imp = mean(abortion)
  )

# Calculate pooled estimates
pooled_live <- mean(age_45_imputed$live_birth_imp)
pooled_abortion <- mean(age_45_imputed$abortion_imp)

# Update the original data with imputed values
henry_data$live_birth[5] <- round(pooled_live, 2)
henry_data$abortion[5] <- round(pooled_abortion, 2)

cat("\nImputation results for age 45-49:\n")
cat("Live birth proportion unintended:", henry_data$live_birth[5], "\n")
cat("Abortion proportion unintended:", henry_data$abortion[5], "\n")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 3: Pregnancy outcome distribution from Norwegian registry study
#===========================================================================

# Data from Nordeng et al. (2024) - UiO pregnancy algorithm
# Overall distribution of pregnancy outcomes in Norway 2008-2018
norway_pregnancy_dist <- data.frame(
  outcome = c("live_birth", "miscarriage", "abortion", "ectopic"),
  proportion = c(0.748, 0.131, 0.110, 0.007)  # From paper: 74.8%, 13.1%, 11.0%, 0.7%
)

print(norway_pregnancy_dist)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 4: Function to calculate conditional probabilities for one age group
#=============================================================================

calculate_age_probabilities <- function(live_prop, abort_prop) {
  
  # Step 1: Multiply each outcome by its "proportion unintended"
  # Miscarriage and ectopic use 0.5 (Henry's assumption, also used in Nordeng et al.)
  numerators <- c(
    live_birth = norway_pregnancy_dist$proportion[1] * live_prop,
    abortion = norway_pregnancy_dist$proportion[3] * abort_prop,
    miscarriage = norway_pregnancy_dist$proportion[2] * 0.5,
    ectopic = norway_pregnancy_dist$proportion[4] * 0.5
  )
  
  # Step 2: Calculate sum for normalization
  total <- sum(numerators)
  
  # Step 3: Divide each by total to get probabilities (sum to 1)
  probabilities <- numerators / total
  
  # Step 4: Convert to percentages
  percentages <- round(probabilities * 100, 1)
  
  return(list(probabilities = probabilities, 
              percentages = percentages,
              total = total))
}

#===========================================================================
# STEP 5: Calculate for each age group
#===========================================================================

results <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(henry_data)) {
  age_group <- henry_data$age_group[i]
  results[[age_group]] <- calculate_age_probabilities(
    henry_data$live_birth[i], 
    henry_data$abortion[i]
  )
}

# Build the final table
final_table <- data.frame(
  age_group = henry_data$age_group,
  live_birth_unintended = henry_data$live_birth,
  abortion_unintended = henry_data$abortion,
  live_birth_pct = sapply(henry_data$age_group, 
                          function(x) results[[x]]$percentages[1]),
  abortion_pct = sapply(henry_data$age_group, 
                        function(x) results[[x]]$percentages[2]),
  miscarriage_pct = sapply(henry_data$age_group, 
                           function(x) results[[x]]$percentages[3]),
  ectopic_pct = sapply(henry_data$age_group, 
                       function(x) results[[x]]$percentages[4])
)

# Add a check column (should sum to ~100%)
final_table$check_sum <- rowSums(final_table[, 4:7])

cat("\n======================================================================\n")
cat("FINAL RESULTS: Conditional Probabilities (%)\n")
cat("(Given that an unintended pregnancy has occurred)\n")
cat("======================================================================\n\n")
print(final_table)

#===========================================================================
# STEP 6: Calculate Alpha and Beta parameters for Dirichlet distribution
#===========================================================================

# Extract probabilities as decimals.
# we use unrounded probabilities from results list — NOT the rounded percentagesmin final_table — to avoid accumulating rounding error in model parameters.
probs_data <- data.frame(
  age_group     = henry_data$age_group,
  p_live        = sapply(henry_data$age_group, function(x) results[[x]]$probabilities[1]),
  p_abortion    = sapply(henry_data$age_group, function(x) results[[x]]$probabilities[2]),
  p_miscarriage = sapply(henry_data$age_group, function(x) results[[x]]$probabilities[3]),
  p_ectopic     = sapply(henry_data$age_group, function(x) results[[x]]$probabilities[4])
)

# Verify each row sums to 1 (should be exact, not 99.9/100.1)
probs_data$check_sum <- rowSums(probs_data[, 2:5])
cat("\nProbability check (should be exactly 1.00):\n")
print(probs_data[, c("age_group", "check_sum")])

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dirichlet alpha parameters — based on actual Nordeng et al. registry counts
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

nordeng_counts <- c(
  live_birth   = 642712,
  abortion     = 94664,
  miscarriage  = 112257,
  ectopic      = 6429
)
nordeng_total <- sum(nordeng_counts)
cat("\nNordeng et al. registry counts (Dirichlet prior):\n")
print(nordeng_counts)
cat("Total:", nordeng_total, "\n")

# Scale alpha parameters: for each age group, scale the Nordeng counts
# by the age-specific conditional probabilities. This preserves the registry
# precision while incorporating age-specific unintendedness from Henry et al.
alpha_table <- probs_data %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_live        = p_live        * nordeng_total,
    alpha_abortion    = p_abortion    * nordeng_total,
    alpha_miscarriage = p_miscarriage * nordeng_total,
    alpha_ectopic     = p_ectopic     * nordeng_total
  )

cat("\nAlpha parameters (Dirichlet, scaled from Nordeng registry N =",
    nordeng_total, "):\n")
print(alpha_table[, c("age_group", "alpha_live", "alpha_abortion",
                      "alpha_miscarriage", "alpha_ectopic")])

#=============================================================================
# STEP 7: Calculate 95% Confidence Intervals (Marginal Beta distributions)
#=============================================================================
# N = nordeng_total (855,062) — consistent with Dirichlet alpha parameters 

calculate_beta_ci <- function(p, N = nordeng_total) {
  alpha <- p * N
  beta  <- (1 - p) * N
  lower <- qbeta(0.025, alpha, beta)
  upper <- qbeta(0.975, alpha, beta)
  return(list(lower = lower, upper = upper, alpha = alpha, beta = beta))
}

# Calculate for each probability
ci_results <- list()
for(i in 1:nrow(probs_data)) {
  age <- probs_data$age_group[i]

  ci_live        <- calculate_beta_ci(probs_data$p_live[i])
  ci_abortion    <- calculate_beta_ci(probs_data$p_abortion[i])
  ci_miscarriage <- calculate_beta_ci(probs_data$p_miscarriage[i])
  ci_ectopic     <- calculate_beta_ci(probs_data$p_ectopic[i])
  
  ci_results[[age]] <- data.frame(
    outcome = c("live", "abortion", "miscarriage", "ectopic"),
    probability = c(probs_data$p_live[i], probs_data$p_abortion[i],
                    probs_data$p_miscarriage[i], probs_data$p_ectopic[i]),
    alpha = c(ci_live$alpha, ci_abortion$alpha, ci_miscarriage$alpha, ci_ectopic$alpha),
    beta = c(ci_live$beta, ci_abortion$beta, ci_miscarriage$beta, ci_ectopic$beta),
    ci_lower = c(ci_live$lower, ci_abortion$lower, ci_miscarriage$lower, ci_ectopic$lower),
    ci_upper = c(ci_live$upper, ci_abortion$upper, ci_miscarriage$upper, ci_ectopic$upper)
  )
}

cat("\n95% Confidence Intervals (Marginal Beta distributions):\n")
for(age in names(ci_results)) {
  cat(paste("\nAge", age, ":\n"))
  print(ci_results[[age]])
}

#=============================================================================
# STEP 8: Generate Dirichlet samples for Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis
#=============================================================================

set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility

# Function to generate Dirichlet samples for one age group
generate_dirichlet_psa <- function(alphas, n_samples = 1000) {
  # alphas: vector of 4 concentration parameters
  samples <- rdirichlet(n_samples, alphas)
  colnames(samples) <- c("live", "abortion", "miscarriage", "ectopic")
  return(samples)
}

# Generate PSA samples for each age group
psa_samples <- list()
n_psa <- 1000  # Number of PSA iterations

for(i in 1:nrow(alpha_table)) {
  age <- alpha_table$age_group[i]
  
  # Get the 4 alpha parameters for this age group
  alphas <- c(alpha_table$alpha_live[i],
              alpha_table$alpha_abortion[i],
              alpha_table$alpha_miscarriage[i],
              alpha_table$alpha_ectopic[i])
  
  # Generate Dirichlet samples
  samples <- generate_dirichlet_psa(alphas, n_psa)
  psa_samples[[age]] <- samples
  
  # Check: mean should be close to original probabilities
  cat(paste("\nAge", age, "- PSA validation:\n"))
  cat(sprintf("  Original: Live=%.3f, Ab=%.3f, Misc=%.3f, Ect=%.3f\n",
              probs_data$p_live[i], probs_data$p_abortion[i],
              probs_data$p_miscarriage[i], probs_data$p_ectopic[i]))
  cat(sprintf("  PSA mean: Live=%.3f, Ab=%.3f, Misc=%.3f, Ect=%.3f\n",
              mean(samples[,1]), mean(samples[,2]),
              mean(samples[,3]), mean(samples[,4])))
  cat(sprintf("  Sum to 1? %s (min=%.4f, max=%.4f)\n",
              all(round(rowSums(samples), 10) == 1),
              min(rowSums(samples)), max(rowSums(samples))))
}

#=============================================================================
# STEP 9: Create final PSA parameter table
#=============================================================================

final_psa_table <- data.frame()

for(age in names(ci_results)) {
  age_data <- ci_results[[age]]
  
  for(j in 1:nrow(age_data)) {
    row <- data.frame(
      age_group = age,
      outcome = age_data$outcome[j],
      probability = round(age_data$probability[j], 4),
      alpha = round(age_data$alpha[j], 1),
      beta = round(age_data$beta[j], 1),
      ci_95 = sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", age_data$ci_lower[j], age_data$ci_upper[j])
    )
    final_psa_table <- rbind(final_psa_table, row)
  }
}

cat("\n======================================================================\n")
cat("FINAL PSA PARAMETERS FOR MARKOV MODEL\n")
cat("Age groups: 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49\n")
cat("======================================================================\n\n")
print(final_psa_table)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 10: Export tables for manuscript
#=============================================================================

# Create manuscript table (simplified) — use unrounded probabilities,
# format percentages for display only here
manuscript_up_table <- data.frame(
  `Age group`          = final_table$age_group,
  `Live birth (%)`     = round(probs_data$p_live        * 100, 1),
  `Induced abortion (%)` = round(probs_data$p_abortion  * 100, 1),
  `Miscarriage (%)`    = round(probs_data$p_miscarriage  * 100, 1),
  `Ectopic (%)`        = round(probs_data$p_ectopic      * 100, 1),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Word document table
ft_up_probs <- flextable(manuscript_up_table) |>
  set_caption("Table 2. Conditional probabilities of unintended pregnancy outcomes by age group (%)") |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
  align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
  align(align = "left",   j = 1, part = "body") |>
  align(align = "center", j = -1, part = "body") |>
  bg(bg = "#1B3A6B", part = "header") |>
  color(color = "white", part = "header") |>
  border_outer(part = "all") |>
  border_inner_h(part = "body") |>
  autofit()

save_as_docx(ft_up_probs,
             path = "Table2_UP_Conditional_Probabilities.docx")
cat("Table 2 saved as Table2_UP_Conditional_Probabilities.docx\n")

# Save full PSA parameters as CSV (for record)
write.csv(final_psa_table,
          file = "Appendix_UP_PSA_Parameters.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("PSA parameters saved as Appendix_UP_PSA_Parameters.csv\n")
```

```{r params_probs}
# --- Failure rates (annual, base case) ---
p_fail_fembloc <- 9 / 207        # 0.0435 | conservative: detected UPs / confirmed occlusions [5]
p_fail_tl      <- 0.0264         # US Medicaid cohort [Schwarz et al., 4]

# --- Decision tree: FemBloc confirmation test (FemChec at 12 weeks) ---
p_confirmed   <- 207 / 228       # 0.908 | completed FemChec -> enter PC state [5]
p_unconfirmed <- 1 - p_confirmed # 0.092 | failed confirmation -> enter UP state immediately

cat("FemBloc annual fail rate:    ", round(p_fail_fembloc, 4), "\n")
cat("TL annual fail rate:         ", round(p_fail_tl, 4), "\n")
```

## 2.5 Utility Values

```{r params_utilities}
# --- Health state utilities ---
u_pc  <- 0.8136  # Permanent contraception state | avg Norwegian EQ-5D-5L, women 18-49 [15]
u_up  <- 0.489  # Unintended pregnancy state | Schwartz et al. [16]

# --- AE disutilities (applied in cycle 1 only; AEs resolve within 3 months) ---
u_ae_fembloc <- 0.002627013   # calculated: sum(p_ae * disutility_weight) for FemBloc AEs
u_ae_tl      <- 0.000410507   # calculated: sum(p_ae * disutility_weight) for TL AEs

# 1. PC STATE UTILITY
# Norwegian EQ-5D-5L population norms, weighted average of 3 age groups [15]
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
u_pc_data <- data.frame(
  age_group = c("18-29", "30-39", "40-49"),
  n         = c(317,     272,     272),
  mean      = c(0.825,   0.828,   0.786),
  sd        = c(0.211,   0.208,   0.223)
)

# Weighted mean
total_n    <- sum(u_pc_data$n)
u_pc_mean  <- sum(u_pc_data$n * u_pc_data$mean) / total_n

# Pooled variance and SD
var_pooled <- sum(u_pc_data$n * (u_pc_data$sd^2 + u_pc_data$mean^2)) /
              total_n - u_pc_mean^2
sd_pooled  <- sqrt(var_pooled)

# SE of weighted mean
se_u_pc <- sd_pooled / sqrt(total_n)

# Beta parameters via method of moments
var_u_pc   <- se_u_pc^2
kappa_pc   <- (u_pc_mean * (1 - u_pc_mean) / var_u_pc) - 1
alpha_u_pc <- u_pc_mean * kappa_pc
beta_u_pc  <- (1 - u_pc_mean) * kappa_pc

cat("=== PC STATE UTILITY ===\n")
cat("Weighted mean:  ", round(u_pc_mean,  4), "\n")
cat("Pooled SD:      ", round(sd_pooled,  4), "\n")
cat("SE:             ", round(se_u_pc,    6), "\n")
cat("Alpha:          ", round(alpha_u_pc, 2), "\n")
cat("Beta:           ", round(beta_u_pc,  2), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [",
    round(qbeta(0.025, alpha_u_pc, beta_u_pc), 4), ",",
    round(qbeta(0.975, alpha_u_pc, beta_u_pc), 4), "]\n\n")

# Update u_pc to weighted mean
u_pc <- u_pc_mean

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. UP STATE UTILITY
# Schwartz et al. [16] | mean = 0.489, N = 192
# SE back-calculated from reported margin of error <= 7% at 95% CI
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
u_up_mean  <- 0.489
n_up       <- 192
me_up      <- 0.07 * u_up_mean     # 7% margin of error
se_u_up    <- me_up / 1.96         # back-calculate SE

# Beta parameters via method of moments
var_u_up   <- se_u_up^2
kappa_up   <- (u_up_mean * (1 - u_up_mean) / var_u_up) - 1
alpha_u_up <- u_up_mean * kappa_up
beta_u_up  <- (1 - u_up_mean) * kappa_up

cat("=== UP STATE UTILITY ===\n")
cat("Mean:           ", round(u_up_mean,  4), "\n")
cat("Margin of error:", round(me_up,      4), "\n")
cat("SE:             ", round(se_u_up,    6), "\n")
cat("Alpha:          ", round(alpha_u_up, 2), "\n")
cat("Beta:           ", round(beta_u_up,  2), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [",
    round(qbeta(0.025, alpha_u_up, beta_u_up), 4), ",",
    round(qbeta(0.975, alpha_u_up, beta_u_up), 4), "]\n\n")

# Update u_up
u_up <- u_up_mean

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. SUMMARY TABLE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
utility_params <- data.frame(
  Parameter    = c("u_pc (PC state)", "u_up (UP state)"),
  Mean         = round(c(u_pc_mean,  u_up_mean),  4),
  SE           = round(c(se_u_pc,    se_u_up),    6),
  Alpha        = round(c(alpha_u_pc, alpha_u_up), 2),
  Beta         = round(c(beta_u_pc,  beta_u_up),  2),
  CI_low       = round(c(qbeta(0.025, alpha_u_pc, beta_u_pc),
                         qbeta(0.025, alpha_u_up, beta_u_up)), 4),
  CI_high      = round(c(qbeta(0.975, alpha_u_pc, beta_u_pc),
                         qbeta(0.975, alpha_u_up, beta_u_up)), 4),
  Distribution = c("Beta", "Beta")
)

kable(utility_params,
      caption = "Utility distribution parameters for PSA") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# Save for use in PSA
save.image("fembloc_utility_params.RData")

```

# =============================================================================
# MARKOV LOOP
# =============================================================================

```{r}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fecundity ratio for a given age (maps to 5-year band)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
get_fr <- function(age) {
  if      (age < 30) fr$fr_mean[fr$group == "25-29"]
  else if (age < 35) fr$fr_mean[fr$group == "30-34"]
  else if (age < 40) fr$fr_mean[fr$group == "35-39"]
  else if (age < 45) fr$fr_mean[fr$group == "40-44"]
  else               fr$fr_mean[fr$group == "45-50"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# UP state cost for a given age (maps to 5-year band)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
get_up_cost <- function(age) {
  if      (age < 30) up_state_cost_by_age["25-29"]
  else if (age < 35) up_state_cost_by_age["30-34"]
  else if (age < 40) up_state_cost_by_age["35-39"]
  else if (age < 45) up_state_cost_by_age["40-44"]
  else               up_state_cost_by_age["45-50"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CORE FUNCTION: run Markov model for one age group, one arm
# Returns vectors of discounted costs and QALYs per cycle
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_markov <- function(arm, ag) {
  
  horizon   <- ag$horizon       # years to age 50
  mid_age   <- ag$midpoint      # starting age (midpoint of band)
  disc_r    <- ag$disc_rate     # discount rate (4% or 3%)
  
  # --- Procedure cost: applied at cycle 0, undiscounted ---
  proc_cost <- if (arm == "fembloc") fembloc_cost_cycle0 else tl_cost_cycle0
  
  # --- Starting state proportions (post decision tree) ---
  # FemBloc: unconfirmed women (9.2%) enter UP immediately for 1 cycle
  # TL:      all women enter PC
 if (arm == "fembloc") {
    fr_cycle1  <- get_fr(mid_age)
    prop_pc    <- p_confirmed
    prop_up    <- p_unconfirmed * fr_cycle1  # fecundity decay applied to unconfirmed
    prop_pc    <- prop_pc + (p_unconfirmed * (1 - fr_cycle1))  # remainder stay in PC
  } else {
    prop_pc <- 1.0
    prop_up <- 0.0
  }
  
  # --- Storage ---
  costs  <- numeric(horizon)
  qalys  <- numeric(horizon)
  up_vec <- numeric(horizon)   # track UP proportions for validation
  
  for (cycle in 1:horizon) {
    
    # Current age this cycle (midpoint age + cycles elapsed)
    current_age <- mid_age + (cycle - 1)
    
    # Fecundity ratio updates every 5 years as cohort ages through bands
    fr_current <- get_fr(current_age)
    
    # Age-adjusted failure rate
    p_fail     <- if (arm == "fembloc") p_fail_fembloc else p_fail_tl
    p_fail_adj <- p_fail * fr_current
    
    # UP state cost for current age band
    up_cost_current <- get_up_cost(current_age)
    
    # --- Discount factor ---
    disc_factor <- 1 / (1 + disc_r)^cycle
    
    # --- Half-cycle correction ---
    # Applied at cycle 1 and final cycle (0.5), all others = 1.0
    hcc <- if (cycle == 1 || cycle == horizon) 0.5 else 1.0
    
    # --- Utilities this cycle ---
    # AE disutility applied in cycle 1 only (resolves within 3 months)
    u_pc_cycle <- if (cycle == 1) {
      u_pc - if (arm == "fembloc") u_ae_fembloc else u_ae_tl
    } else {
      u_pc
    }
    
    # --- QALYs (discounted + half-cycle corrected) ---
    qaly_cycle    <- (prop_pc * u_pc_cycle + prop_up * u_up) * hcc * disc_factor
    qalys[cycle]  <- qaly_cycle
    
    # --- Costs (discounted) ---
    # Procedure cost added outside loop (cycle 0, undiscounted)
    # UP state cost applied per cycle spent in UP state
    cost_cycle   <- (prop_up * up_cost_current) * disc_factor
    costs[cycle] <- cost_cycle
    
    # --- Store UP proportion for validation ---
    up_vec[cycle] <- prop_up
    
    # --- Transition to next cycle ---
    # PC -> UP with adjusted failure rate
    # PC -> PC with (1 - adjusted failure rate)
    # UP -> PC after 1 cycle (all women return)
    new_up   <- prop_pc * p_fail_adj
    new_pc   <- prop_pc * (1 - p_fail_adj) + prop_up  # UP returns to PC
    
    prop_pc  <- new_pc
    prop_up  <- new_up
  }
  
  list(
    arm        = arm,
    group      = ag$group,
    total_cost = proc_cost + sum(costs),   # cycle 0 + discounted state costs
    total_qaly = sum(qalys),
    cost_vec   = costs,
    qaly_vec   = qalys,
    up_vec     = up_vec                    # for validation
  )
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RUN ALL AGE GROUPS, BOTH ARMS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
results_fembloc <- lapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i) 
  run_markov("fembloc", age_groups[i, ]))

results_tl <- lapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i) 
  run_markov("tl", age_groups[i, ]))

# Name lists for easy reference
names(results_fembloc) <- age_groups$group
names(results_tl)      <- age_groups$group

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AGGREGATE ACROSS AGE GROUPS (weighted by cohort proportions)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
agg_cost_fembloc <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  results_fembloc[[i]]$total_cost * age_groups$prop[i]))

agg_qaly_fembloc <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  results_fembloc[[i]]$total_qaly * age_groups$prop[i]))

agg_cost_tl <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  results_tl[[i]]$total_cost * age_groups$prop[i]))

agg_qaly_tl <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  results_tl[[i]]$total_qaly * age_groups$prop[i]))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INCREMENTAL RESULTS & ICER
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
inc_cost <- agg_cost_fembloc - agg_cost_tl
inc_qaly <- agg_qaly_fembloc - agg_qaly_tl
icer_qaly <- inc_cost / inc_qaly

up_fembloc <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  sum(results_fembloc[[i]]$up_vec) * age_groups$prop[i]))

up_tl <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
  sum(results_tl[[i]]$up_vec) * age_groups$prop[i]))

inc_up_markov <- up_fembloc - up_tl
icer_up       <- inc_cost / inc_up_markov # NOK per UP avoided (per average woman scale)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SUMMARY TABLE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
base_case_summary <- data.frame(
  Strategy      = c("FemBloc", "Tubal Ligation", "Incremental"),
  Total_Cost    = round(c(agg_cost_fembloc, agg_cost_tl, inc_cost), 0),
  Total_QALYs   = round(c(agg_qaly_fembloc, agg_qaly_tl, inc_qaly), 4),
  UPs = round(c(up_fembloc, up_tl, -(up_fembloc - up_tl)), 1),
  ICER_per_QALY = c(NA, NA, round(icer_qaly, 0)),
  ICER_per_UP   = c(NA, NA, round(icer_up, 0))
)

cat("==================== BASE CASE RESULTS ====================\n")
print(base_case_summary)
cat("\nICER (NOK per QALY gained):        ", round(icer_qaly, 0), "\n")
cat("ICER (NOK per UP avoided):         ", round(icer_up, 0), "\n")

kable(base_case_summary,
      caption = "Base Case Cost-Effectiveness Results (NOK 2026)",
      col.names = c("Strategy", "Total Cost (NOK)",
                    "Total QALYs", "UPs", 
                    "ICER/QALY (NOK)", "ICER/UP avoided (NOK)")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VALIDATION: UP proportions per cycle (age group 35-39, largest share)
# Compare against ~39,000 UP/year in Norway [3]
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n--- VALIDATION: UP proportions per cycle (35-39 group) ---\n")
cat("FemBloc UP proportions:\n")
print(round(results_fembloc[["35-39"]]$up_vec, 4))
cat("TL UP proportions:\n")
print(round(results_tl[["35-39"]]$up_vec, 4))

# Save results
save.image("fembloc_markov.RData")
```

```{r}
dur_pain_fb_yrs <- 7  / 365

# TL components

disut_pid       <- 0.15

sd_pid          <- 0.315        # Pillay et al. [23]

dur_pain_tl_yrs <- 7  / 365

# Verify base case totals match parameters chunk

                 (p_pain_fb     * disut_pain_fb  * dur_pain_fb_yrs)
u_ae_tl_check <- (p_pid         * disut_pid      * dur_pid_yrs)    +
                 (p_pain_tl     * disut_pain_tl  * dur_pain_tl_yrs)

cat("u_ae_tl check (should be 0.000411):     ", round(u_ae_tl_check, 6), "\n")

# DSA bounds
u_ae_fb_lo <- (p_perforation * (disut_perf   * 0.90) * dur_perf_yrs)    +
              (p_pain_fb     * (disut_pain_fb * 0.90) * dur_pain_fb_yrs)
u_ae_fb_hi <- (p_perforation * (disut_perf   * 1.10) * dur_perf_yrs)    +
              (p_pain_fb     * (disut_pain_fb * 1.10) * dur_pain_fb_yrs)

u_ae_tl_lo <- (p_pid     * max(0, disut_pid - 1.96 * sd_pid) * dur_pid_yrs) +
              (p_pain_tl * (disut_pain_tl * 0.90)            * dur_pain_tl_yrs)
u_ae_tl_hi <- (p_pid     * min(1, disut_pid + 1.96 * sd_pid) * dur_pid_yrs) +
              (p_pain_tl * (disut_pain_tl * 1.10)            * dur_pain_tl_yrs)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Full model with parameter overrides
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_dsa <- function(
    p_fail_fb     = p_fail_fembloc,
    p_fail_tl_dsa = p_fail_tl,
    cost_fb_total = fembloc_cost_cycle0,
    cost_tl_total = tl_cost_cycle0,
    u_ae_fb       = u_ae_fembloc,
    u_ae_tl_dsa   = u_ae_tl
) {

  run_arm <- function(arm, ag) {
    horizon   <- ag$horizon
    mid_age   <- ag$midpoint
    disc_r    <- ag$disc_rate
    p_fail    <- if (arm == "fembloc") p_fail_fb else p_fail_tl_dsa
    proc_cost <- if (arm == "fembloc") cost_fb_total else cost_tl_total

    fr_cycle1 <- get_fr(mid_age)

    if (arm == "fembloc") {
      prop_pc <- p_confirmed + (p_unconfirmed * (1 - fr_cycle1))
      prop_up <- p_unconfirmed * fr_cycle1
    } else {
      prop_pc <- 1.0
      prop_up <- 0.0
    }

    costs <- numeric(horizon)
    qalys <- numeric(horizon)

    for (cycle in 1:horizon) {
      current_age     <- mid_age + (cycle - 1)
      fr_current      <- get_fr(current_age)
      p_fail_adj      <- p_fail * fr_current
      up_cost_current <- up_state_cost_by_age[
        ifelse(current_age < 30, "25-29",
        ifelse(current_age < 35, "30-34",
        ifelse(current_age < 40, "35-39",
        ifelse(current_age < 45, "40-44", "45-50"))))]

      disc_factor <- 1 / (1 + disc_r)^cycle
      hcc         <- if (cycle == 1 || cycle == horizon) 0.5 else 1.0

      u_pc_cycle  <- if (cycle == 1) {
        u_pc - if (arm == "fembloc") u_ae_fb else u_ae_tl_dsa
      } else u_pc

      qalys[cycle] <- (prop_pc * u_pc_cycle + prop_up * u_up) * hcc * disc_factor
      costs[cycle] <- (prop_up * up_cost_current) * disc_factor

      new_up  <- prop_pc * p_fail_adj
      prop_pc <- prop_pc * (1 - p_fail_adj) + prop_up
      prop_up <- new_up
    }

    list(total_cost = proc_cost + sum(costs),
         total_qaly = sum(qalys))
  }

  cost_fb <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
    run_arm("fembloc", age_groups[i,])$total_cost * age_groups$prop[i]))
  qaly_fb <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
    run_arm("fembloc", age_groups[i,])$total_qaly * age_groups$prop[i]))
  cost_tl <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
    run_arm("tl", age_groups[i,])$total_cost * age_groups$prop[i]))
  qaly_tl <- sum(sapply(1:nrow(age_groups), function(i)
    run_arm("tl", age_groups[i,])$total_qaly * age_groups$prop[i]))

  (cost_fb - cost_tl) / (qaly_fb - qaly_tl)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RUN DSA — one parameter at a time
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
dsa_results <- data.frame(
  parameter = character(),
  icer_low  = numeric(),
  icer_high = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

add_dsa <- function(name, icer_lo, icer_hi) {
  dsa_results <<- rbind(dsa_results, data.frame(
    parameter = name,
    icer_low  = round(icer_lo),
    icer_high = round(icer_hi)
  ))
}

add_dsa("FemBloc costs",
        run_dsa(cost_fb_total = fb_cost_lo),
        run_dsa(cost_fb_total = fb_cost_hi))

add_dsa("TL costs",
        run_dsa(cost_tl_total = tl_cost_lo),
        run_dsa(cost_tl_total = tl_cost_hi))

add_dsa("FemBloc fail rate",
        run_dsa(p_fail_fb = fembloc_fail_lo),
        run_dsa(p_fail_fb = fembloc_fail_hi))

add_dsa("TL fail rate",
        run_dsa(p_fail_tl_dsa = tl_fail_lo),
        run_dsa(p_fail_tl_dsa = tl_fail_hi))

add_dsa("FemBloc AE disutility",
        run_dsa(u_ae_fb = u_ae_fb_lo),
        run_dsa(u_ae_fb = u_ae_fb_hi))

add_dsa("TL AE disutility",
        run_dsa(u_ae_tl_dsa = u_ae_tl_lo),
        run_dsa(u_ae_tl_dsa = u_ae_tl_hi))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

dsa_results$swing <- abs(dsa_results$icer_high - dsa_results$icer_low)

cat("\n========== DSA RESULTS (ICER NOK/QALY) ==========\n")

# Low labels — to the LEFT of the dot
geom_text(aes(x = low_plot - 8000,

# High labels — to the RIGHT of the dot
```

```{r psa, cache=TRUE}

library(MCMCpack)  # for rdirichlet

set.seed(123)
n_sim <- 10000

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DISTRIBUTION PARAMETERS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Costs: Gamma(alpha, rate) | rate = alpha / mean ---
# Gamma mean = alpha/rate, so rate = alpha/mean
gamma_rate <- function(alpha, mean) alpha / mean

# FemBloc
g_device_a   <- 6;      g_device_m   <- 11350
g_premed_fb_a <- 25;    g_premed_fb_m <- 506
g_postmed_fb_a <- 25;   g_postmed_fb_m <- 17

# TL
g_premed_tl_a <- 25;    g_premed_tl_m <- 1622
g_postmed_tl_a <- 25;   g_postmed_tl_m <- 71

# --- Probabilities: Beta(alpha, beta) ---
# Fail rates
a_fail_fb  <- 10;   b_fail_fb  <- 199    # FemBloc fail rate
a_fail_tl  <- 633;  b_fail_tl  <- 23325  # TL fail rate

# Confirmation rate
a_confirm  <- 207;  b_confirm  <- 21     # FemChec -> PC

# --- Utilities: Beta(alpha, beta) ---
a_u_pc <- 2302.31;  b_u_pc <- 527.38    # PC state
a_u_up <- 400.13;   b_u_up <- 418.14    # UP state

# --- AE disutility components ---
# FemBloc: perforation and pelvic pain (±10% on disutility weights)
# Sampled as Beta on the disutility weight itself

se_disut_perf  <- 0.049
se_disut_pain  <- 0.035

mom_beta <- function(mean, se) {
  var   <- se^2
  kappa <- (mean * (1 - mean) / var) - 1
  list(alpha = mean * kappa, beta = (1 - mean) * kappa)
}

b_perf <- mom_beta(0.49, se_disut_perf)
b_pain <- mom_beta(0.35, se_disut_pain)

# TL: PID disutility (SE=0.315 from Pillay et al.), pelvic pain ±10%
b_pid  <- mom_beta(min(0.15, 0.999), 0.315)   # wide uncertainty
b_pain_tl <- mom_beta(0.35, se_disut_pain)

# --- Fecundity ratios: Log-normal(log_mu, log_sigma) ---

fr_log_mu    <- setNames(band_summary$logFR_mean, age_groups$group)
fr_log_sigma <- setNames(sqrt(band_summary$logFR_var), age_groups$group)

# --- UP outcome probabilities: Dirichlet ---
# Alpha = probability * nordeng_total (actual registry counts from Nordeng et al.-855062)

up_dir_alpha <- up_probs * nordeng_total   # 5 x 4 matrix of Dirichlet alphas

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. PSA DRAW FUNCTION
# Samples all parameters once, returns named list
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
draw_psa_params <- function() {

  # --- Costs ---
  d_device    <- rgamma(1, shape = g_device_a,
                        rate  = gamma_rate(g_device_a, g_device_m))
  d_premed_fb <- rgamma(1, shape = g_premed_fb_a,
                        rate  = gamma_rate(g_premed_fb_a, g_premed_fb_m))
  d_postmed_fb <- rgamma(1, shape = g_postmed_fb_a,
                         rate  = gamma_rate(g_postmed_fb_a, g_postmed_fb_m))
  d_premed_tl  <- rgamma(1, shape = g_premed_tl_a,
                         rate  = gamma_rate(g_premed_tl_a, g_premed_tl_m))
  d_postmed_tl <- rgamma(1, shape = g_postmed_tl_a,
                         rate  = gamma_rate(g_postmed_tl_a, g_postmed_tl_m))

  # Recompute cycle 0 costs with sampled components
  fb_cost <- d_device      +
             d_premed_fb   +
             d_postmed_fb  +
             fembloc_insertion_fee   +   # fixed
             fembloc_ultrasound_cost +   # fixed
             fembloc_consult_cost    +   # fixed
             ae_cost_fembloc         +   # fixed
             fembloc_travel_leisure      # fixed

  tl_cost <- tl_procedure_cost  +        # fixed
             d_premed_tl        +
             d_postmed_tl       +
             ae_cost_tl         +        # fixed
             tl_travel_leisure           # fixed

  # --- Probabilities ---
  p_fail_fb_s  <- rbeta(1, a_fail_fb,  b_fail_fb)
  p_fail_tl_s  <- rbeta(1, a_fail_tl,  b_fail_tl)
  p_confirm_s  <- rbeta(1, a_confirm,  b_confirm)
  p_unconfirm_s <- 1 - p_confirm_s

  # --- Utilities ---
  u_pc_s <- rbeta(1, a_u_pc, b_u_pc)
  u_up_s <- rbeta(1, a_u_up, b_u_up)

  # --- AE disutilities ---
  disut_perf_s    <- rbeta(1, b_perf$alpha, b_perf$beta)
  disut_pain_fb_s <- rbeta(1, b_pain$alpha, b_pain$beta)
  disut_pid_s     <- rbeta(1, b_pid$alpha,  b_pid$beta)
  disut_pain_tl_s <- rbeta(1, b_pain_tl$alpha, b_pain_tl$beta)

  u_ae_fb_s <- (p_perforation * disut_perf_s    * dur_perf_yrs)    +
               (p_pain_fb     * disut_pain_fb_s  * dur_pain_fb_yrs)
  u_ae_tl_s <- (p_pid         * disut_pid_s      * dur_pid_yrs)    +
               (p_pain_tl     * disut_pain_tl_s  * dur_pain_tl_yrs)

  # --- Fecundity ratios ---
  fr_s <- setNames(
    rlnorm(5, meanlog = fr_log_mu, sdlog = fr_log_sigma),
    age_groups$group
  )

  # --- UP outcome probabilities: Dirichlet per age group ---
  up_probs_s <- matrix(NA, nrow = 5, ncol = 4,
                       dimnames = dimnames(up_probs))
  for (i in 1:5) {
    up_probs_s[i, ] <- rdirichlet(1, up_dir_alpha[i, ])
  }

  # Recompute UP state costs with sampled probabilities
  outcome_costs_s <- c(cost_live_birth, cost_induced_abortion,
                       cost_miscarriage, cost_ectopic_pregnancy)
  up_costs_s <- as.vector(up_probs_s %*% outcome_costs_s)
  names(up_costs_s) <- age_groups$group

  list(
    fb_cost       = fb_cost,
    tl_cost       = tl_cost,
    p_fail_fb     = p_fail_fb_s,
    p_fail_tl     = p_fail_tl_s,
    p_confirm     = p_confirm_s,
    p_unconfirm   = p_unconfirm_s,
    u_pc          = u_pc_s,
    u_up          = u_up_s,
    u_ae_fb       = u_ae_fb_s,
    u_ae_tl       = u_ae_tl_s,
    fr            = fr_s,
    up_costs      = up_costs_s
  )
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. PSA MARKOV FUNCTION
# Runs one arm for one age group using sampled parameters
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_psa_arm <- function(arm, ag, p) {

  horizon   <- ag$horizon
  mid_age   <- ag$midpoint
  disc_r    <- ag$disc_rate
  p_fail    <- if (arm == "fembloc") p$p_fail_fb else p$p_fail_tl
  proc_cost <- if (arm == "fembloc") p$fb_cost   else p$tl_cost

  grp_start <- ag$group
  fr_cycle1 <- p$fr[grp_start]

  if (arm == "fembloc") {
    prop_pc <- p$p_confirm   + (p$p_unconfirm * (1 - fr_cycle1))
    prop_up <- p$p_unconfirm * fr_cycle1
  } else {
    prop_pc <- 1.0
    prop_up <- 0.0
  }

  costs <- numeric(horizon)
  qalys <- numeric(horizon)
  ups   <- numeric(horizon)

  for (cycle in 1:horizon) {
    current_age <- mid_age + (cycle - 1)

    current_grp <- ifelse(current_age < 30, "25-29",
                   ifelse(current_age < 35, "30-34",
                   ifelse(current_age < 40, "35-39",
                   ifelse(current_age < 45, "40-44", "45-50"))))

    fr_current  <- p$fr[current_grp]
    p_fail_adj  <- p_fail * fr_current
    up_cost_now <- p$up_costs[current_grp]

    disc_factor <- 1 / (1 + disc_r)^cycle
    hcc         <- if (cycle == 1 || cycle == horizon) 0.5 else 1.0

    u_pc_cycle  <- if (cycle == 1) {
      p$u_pc - if (arm == "fembloc") p$u_ae_fb else p$u_ae_tl
    } else p$u_pc

    ups[cycle]   <- prop_up                              # track UP occupancy
    qalys[cycle] <- (prop_pc * u_pc_cycle + prop_up * p$u_up) *
                     hcc * disc_factor
    costs[cycle] <- (prop_up * up_cost_now) * disc_factor

    new_up  <- prop_pc * p_fail_adj
    prop_pc <- prop_pc * (1 - p_fail_adj) + prop_up
    prop_up <- new_up
  }

  list(cost = proc_cost + sum(costs),
       qaly = sum(qalys),
       up   = sum(ups))
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. RUN PSA
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Running", n_sim, "PSA simulations...\n")
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = n_sim, style = 3)

# Storage: aggregated results
psa_cost_fb  <- numeric(n_sim)
psa_cost_tl  <- numeric(n_sim)
psa_qaly_fb  <- numeric(n_sim)
psa_qaly_tl  <- numeric(n_sim)
psa_up_fb    <- numeric(n_sim)  
psa_up_tl    <- numeric(n_sim)



# Storage: by age group (for INMB and EVPPI)
psa_age_cost_fb <- matrix(NA, n_sim, nrow(age_groups),
                           dimnames = list(NULL, age_groups$group))
psa_age_cost_tl <- matrix(NA, n_sim, nrow(age_groups),
                           dimnames = list(NULL, age_groups$group))
psa_age_qaly_fb <- matrix(NA, n_sim, nrow(age_groups),
                           dimnames = list(NULL, age_groups$group))
psa_age_qaly_tl <- matrix(NA, n_sim, nrow(age_groups),
                           dimnames = list(NULL, age_groups$group))

for (s in 1:n_sim) {

  p <- draw_psa_params()

  for (i in 1:nrow(age_groups)) {
    ag <- age_groups[i, ]
    fb <- run_psa_arm("fembloc", ag, p)
    tl <- run_psa_arm("tl",      ag, p)

    psa_age_cost_fb[s, i] <- fb$cost
    psa_age_cost_tl[s, i] <- tl$cost
    psa_age_qaly_fb[s, i] <- fb$qaly
    psa_age_qaly_tl[s, i] <- tl$qaly
    psa_up_fb[s] <- psa_up_fb[s] + fb$up * ag$prop
    psa_up_tl[s] <- psa_up_tl[s] + tl$up * ag$prop
  }

  # Weighted aggregate
  psa_cost_fb[s] <- sum(psa_age_cost_fb[s, ] * age_groups$prop)
  psa_cost_tl[s] <- sum(psa_age_cost_tl[s, ] * age_groups$prop)
  psa_qaly_fb[s] <- sum(psa_age_qaly_fb[s, ] * age_groups$prop)
  psa_qaly_tl[s] <- sum(psa_age_qaly_tl[s, ] * age_groups$prop)

  setTxtProgressBar(pb, s)
}
close(pb)

# Incremental results
psa_inc_cost <- psa_cost_fb - psa_cost_tl
psa_inc_qaly <- psa_qaly_fb - psa_qaly_tl
psa_icer     <- psa_inc_cost / psa_inc_qaly
cat("\n\n========== PSA SUMMARY ==========\n")
cat("Mean incremental cost: NOK", round(mean(psa_inc_cost)), "\n")
cat("Mean incremental QALY:", round(mean(psa_inc_qaly), 4), "\n")
cat("Mean ICER:            ", round(mean(psa_icer[is.finite(psa_icer)])), "\n")
cat("% simulations FemBloc cost-effective at NOK 500,000/QALY:",
    round(mean(psa_inc_cost < 500000 * psa_inc_qaly) * 100, 1), "%\n")

psa_inc_up      <- psa_up_fb - psa_up_tl
psa_cost_per_up <- psa_inc_cost / (psa_up_tl - psa_up_fb)

cat("\n========== COST PER UP AVOIDED ==========\n")
total_up_fembloc <- sum(up_fembloc)
total_up_tl      <- sum(up_tl)
cat("Deterministic - Total UPs FemBloc:", round(total_up_fembloc, 2), "\n")
cat("Deterministic - Total UPs TL:     ", round(total_up_tl, 2), "\n")
cat("Deterministic - Cost per UP avoided: NOK",
    round(inc_cost / (total_up_tl - total_up_fembloc), 2), "\n")
cat("PSA Mean inc UPs:            ", round(mean(psa_inc_up), 2), "\n")
cat("PSA Mean cost per UP avoided: NOK",
    round(mean(psa_cost_per_up[is.finite(psa_cost_per_up)]), 2), "\n")
cat("PSA 95% CI: NOK",
    round(quantile(psa_cost_per_up[is.finite(psa_cost_per_up)], 0.025), 2),
    "to",
    round(quantile(psa_cost_per_up[is.finite(psa_cost_per_up)], 0.975), 2), "\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. COST-EFFECTIVENESS PLANE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ce_data <- data.frame(
  inc_cost = psa_inc_cost,
  inc_qaly = psa_inc_qaly
)

# Colour by quadrant
ce_data$quadrant <- ifelse(psa_inc_cost < 0 & psa_inc_qaly >= 0, "Dominant",
                    ifelse(psa_inc_cost >= 0 & psa_inc_qaly >= 0, "More effective, more costly",
                    ifelse(psa_inc_cost < 0 & psa_inc_qaly < 0,  "Less effective, less costly",
                                                                   "Dominated")))

ce_plane <- ggplot(ce_data, aes(x = inc_qaly, y = inc_cost,
                                 color = quadrant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # WTP threshold line (500,000 NOK)
  geom_abline(slope     = 500000,
              intercept = 0,
              linetype  = "dashed",
              color     = "#CC0000",
              linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Base case point
  annotate("point", x = inc_qaly, y = inc_cost,
           color = "#1B3A6B", size = 4, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Dominant"                   = "#2E8B57",
    "More effective, more costly"= "#1B3A6B",
    "Less effective, less costly"= "#FFA500",
    "Dominated"                  = "#CC0000"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "Cost-Effectiveness Plane",
    subtitle = paste0("10,000 PSA simulations | Base case ICER: NOK ",
                      format(round(icer_base), big.mark = ","), " per QALY"),
    x        = "Incremental QALYs (FemBloc\u00ae vs TL)",
    y        = "Incremental Cost (NOK)",
    color    = "Quadrant",
    caption  = "Diamond = base case | Red dashed line = NOK 500,000/QALY threshold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1B3A6B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(ce_plane)
ggsave("fembloc_ce_plane.png", ce_plane, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. COST-EFFECTIVENESS ACCEPTABILITY CURVE (CEAC)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
wtp_seq <- seq(0, 500000, by = 10000)

# Aggregate CEAC
ceac_agg <- sapply(wtp_seq, function(wtp)
  mean((wtp * psa_inc_qaly - psa_inc_cost) > 0))

# CEAC by age group
ceac_by_age <- sapply(age_groups$group, function(grp) {
  i <- which(age_groups$group == grp)
  inc_c <- psa_age_cost_fb[, i] - psa_age_cost_tl[, i]
  inc_q <- psa_age_qaly_fb[, i] - psa_age_qaly_tl[, i]
  sapply(wtp_seq, function(wtp) mean((wtp * inc_q - inc_c) > 0))
})

ceac_df <- data.frame(
  wtp      = wtp_seq,
  Aggregate = ceac_agg
)
ceac_df <- cbind(ceac_df, as.data.frame(ceac_by_age))

# Reshape for plotting
ceac_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(ceac_df,
                                  cols      = -wtp,
                                  names_to  = "group",
                                  values_to = "prob_ce")

# Plot
ceac_plot <- ggplot(ceac_long,
                    aes(x = wtp / 1000, y = prob_ce,
                        color = group,
                        linewidth = ifelse(group == "Aggregate", 1.2, 0.6),
                        linetype  = ifelse(group == "Aggregate",
                                           "solid", "dashed"))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted",
             color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = icer_base / 1000,
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#CC0000",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma,
                     breaks = seq(0, 500, by = 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent,
                     limits = c(0, 1),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Aggregate" = "#1B3A6B",
    "25-29"     = "#4E9AF1",
    "30-34"     = "#2ECC71",
    "35-39"     = "#F39C12",
    "40-44"     = "#9B59B6",
    "45-50"     = "#E74C3C"
  )) +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  scale_linetype_identity() +
  labs(
    title    = "Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curve (CEAC)",
    subtitle = "Probability FemBloc\u00ae is cost-effective vs Tubal Ligation",
    x        = "Willingness-to-Pay Threshold (NOK thousands per QALY)",
    y        = "Probability Cost-Effective",
    color    = "Group",
    caption  = "Red dashed line = base case ICER | Dotted line = 50% threshold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1B3A6B"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(ceac_plot)
ggsave("fembloc_ceac.png", ceac_plot, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# --- CEAF ---
# At each WTP: identify strategy with highest mean NMB
# Report probability that optimal strategy is cost-effective

ceaf_df <- data.frame(
  wtp      = wtp_seq,
  nmb_fb   = sapply(wtp_seq, function(w) mean(w * psa_qaly_fb - psa_cost_fb)),
  nmb_tl   = sapply(wtp_seq, function(w) mean(w * psa_qaly_tl - psa_cost_tl)),
  prob_fb  = ceac_agg,
  prob_tl  = 1 - ceac_agg
)

# Optimal strategy at each WTP
ceaf_df$optimal       <- ifelse(ceaf_df$nmb_fb >= ceaf_df$nmb_tl,
                                 "FemBloc", "TL")
ceaf_df$prob_optimal  <- ifelse(ceaf_df$optimal == "FemBloc",
                                 ceaf_df$prob_fb,
                                 ceaf_df$prob_tl)

ceaf_plot <- ggplot(ceaf_df, aes(x = wtp / 1000)) +

  # CEAC lines (faded background)
  geom_line(aes(y = prob_fb),
            color = "#1B3A6B", linetype = "dashed",
            linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = prob_tl),
            color = "#CC0000", linetype = "dashed",
            linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +

  # CEAF frontier
  geom_line(aes(y = prob_optimal, color = optimal),
            linewidth = 1.2) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = icer_base / 1000,
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50",
             linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5,
             linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50",
             linewidth = 0.5) +

  scale_color_manual(values = c("FemBloc" = "#1B3A6B",
                                 "TL"      = "#CC0000"),
                     name   = "Optimal strategy") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 500, by = 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent,
                     limits = c(0, 1),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +

  labs(
    title    = "Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Frontier (CEAF)",
    subtitle = "Probability that the optimal strategy is cost-effective",
    x        = "Willingness-to-Pay Threshold (NOK thousands per QALY)",
    y        = "Probability Cost-Effective",
    caption  = paste0("Solid line = CEAF (optimal strategy) | ",
                      "Dashed lines = CEAC for each strategy\n",
                      "Grey dashed = base case ICER (NOK ",
                      format(round(icer_base), big.mark=","), "/QALY)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1B3A6B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(ceaf_plot)
ggsave("fembloc_ceaf.png", ceaf_plot, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. INMB BY AGE GROUP AT KEY WTP THRESHOLDS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
wtp_thresholds <- c(100000, 200000, 300000, 500000)

inmb_age <- do.call(rbind, lapply(age_groups$group, function(grp) {
  i     <- which(age_groups$group == grp)
  inc_c <- psa_age_cost_fb[, i] - psa_age_cost_tl[, i]
  inc_q <- psa_age_qaly_fb[, i] - psa_age_qaly_tl[, i]

  do.call(rbind, lapply(wtp_thresholds, function(wtp) {
    inmb <- wtp * inc_q - inc_c
    data.frame(
      Age_Group = grp,
      WTP       = paste0("NOK ", format(wtp, big.mark = ",")),
      Mean_INMB = round(mean(inmb)),
      CI_low    = round(quantile(inmb, 0.025)),
      CI_high   = round(quantile(inmb, 0.975)),
      Prob_CE   = round(mean(inmb > 0) * 100, 1)
    )
  }))
}))

cat("\n========== INMB BY AGE GROUP ==========\n")
print(inmb_age)

rownames(inmb_age) <- NULL
inmb_age$WTP <- paste0("NOK ", format(wtp_thresholds, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))

kable(inmb_age,
      caption = "Incremental Net Monetary Benefit by Age Group (NOK)",
      col.names = c("Age Group", "WTP Threshold",
                    "Mean INMB", "95% CI Low", "95% CI High",
                    "% Cost-Effective")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE) |>
  collapse_rows(columns = 1)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. SAVE

save.image("fembloc_psa.RData")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONVERGENCE CHECK
# Verifies that n=10,000 simulations is sufficient for stable PSA estimates.
# Plots running mean ICER and running % cost-effective at NOK 500,000/QALY.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Running (cumulative) mean ICER — exclude non-finite values
psa_icer_clean <- ifelse(is.finite(psa_icer), psa_icer, NA)
running_icer   <- cumsum(ifelse(is.na(psa_icer_clean), 0, psa_icer_clean)) /
                  cumsum(!is.na(psa_icer_clean))

# Running % cost-effective at NOK 500,000/QALY
wtp_check      <- 500000
running_pce    <- cumsum(psa_inc_cost < wtp_check * psa_inc_qaly) / seq_along(psa_inc_cost)

# Combine into data frame
conv_df <- data.frame(
  sim        = 1:n_sim,
  icer       = running_icer,
  pct_ce     = running_pce * 100
)

# --- Plot 1: Running mean ICER ---
conv_icer <- ggplot(conv_df, aes(x = sim, y = icer)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1B3A6B", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(psa_icer[is.finite(psa_icer)]),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#CC0000", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title    = "PSA Convergence — Running Mean ICER",
    subtitle = "Red dashed line = final mean ICER",
    x        = "Number of simulations",
    y        = "Cumulative mean ICER (NOK/QALY)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1B3A6B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9)
  )

# --- Plot 2: Running % cost-effective ---
conv_pce <- ggplot(conv_df, aes(x = sim, y = pct_ce)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1B3A6B", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = tail(running_pce, 1) * 100,
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#CC0000", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100),
                     breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  labs(
    title    = "PSA Convergence — Running % Cost-Effective",
    subtitle = paste0("WTP = NOK 500,000/QALY | Red dashed = final value (",
                      round(tail(running_pce, 1) * 100, 1), "%)"),
    x        = "Number of simulations",
    y        = "Cumulative % simulations cost-effective"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1B3A6B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9)
  )

print(conv_icer)
print(conv_pce)

ggsave("fembloc_convergence_icer.png", conv_icer,
       width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave("fembloc_convergence_pce.png",  conv_pce,
       width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

cat("Convergence plots saved.\n")
cat("Final running mean ICER:        ", round(tail(running_icer, 1)), "\n")
cat("Final running % cost-effective: ", round(tail(running_pce, 1) * 100, 1), "%\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#Gewekwe simulation here to provide further validity to convergence. i.e comparing first 20% simulations to last 50% simulations + p-values
#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(coda)

# Convert to mcmc objects
cost_mcmc <- mcmc(psa_inc_cost)
qaly_mcmc <- mcmc(psa_inc_qaly)
icer_mcmc <- mcmc(psa_icer[is.finite(psa_icer)])

# Effective sample size
ess_cost <- effectiveSize(cost_mcmc)
ess_qaly <- effectiveSize(qaly_mcmc)
ess_icer <- effectiveSize(icer_mcmc)

# Geweke diagnostic
geweke_cost <- geweke.diag(cost_mcmc)
geweke_qaly <- geweke.diag(qaly_mcmc)
geweke_icer <- geweke.diag(icer_mcmc)

# Monte Carlo standard error
mcse_cost <- sd(psa_inc_cost) / sqrt(ess_cost)
mcse_qaly <- sd(psa_inc_qaly) / sqrt(ess_qaly)
mcse_icer <- sd(psa_icer[is.finite(psa_icer)]) / sqrt(ess_icer)

# Print results
cat("\n=== CONVERGENCE DIAGNOSTICS ===\n")
cat("Effective sample size:\n")
cat("  Cost:", round(ess_cost), "\n")
cat("  QALY:", round(ess_qaly), "\n")
cat("  ICER:", round(ess_icer), "\n\n")

cat("Geweke z-scores (p-values):\n")
cat("  Cost:", round(geweke_cost$z, 2), " (p =", round(2*pnorm(-abs(geweke_cost$z)), 3), ")\n")
cat("  QALY:", round(geweke_qaly$z, 2), " (p =", round(2*pnorm(-abs(geweke_qaly$z)), 3), ")\n")
cat("  ICER:", round(geweke_icer$z, 2), " (p =", round(2*pnorm(-abs(geweke_icer$z)), 3), ")\n\n")

cat("Monte Carlo standard error:\n")
cat("  Cost: NOK", round(mcse_cost, 0), "(", round(mcse_cost/abs(mean(psa_inc_cost))*100, 1), "% of mean)\n")
cat("  QALY:", round(mcse_qaly, 4), "(", round(mcse_qaly/abs(mean(psa_inc_qaly))*100, 1), "% of mean)\n")
cat("  ICER: NOK", round(mcse_icer, 0), "(", round(mcse_icer/abs(mean(psa_icer[is.finite(psa_icer)]))*100, 1), "% of mean)\n")
```

```{r evppi, cache=TRUE, dependson="psa"}
for (s in 1:n_evppi) {

  p <- draw_psa_params()

  # Save draws
  draws$p_fail_fb[s]   <- p$p_fail_fb
  # Device cost drawn directly from Gamma distribution.
  # (A previous version attempted to back-calculate from p$fb_cost,
  #  but that expression was immediately overwritten — removed as dead code.)
  draws$device_cost[s] <- rgamma(1,
                                  shape = g_device_a,
                                  rate  = gamma_rate(g_device_a, g_device_m))
  draws$u_pc[s]        <- p$u_pc
  draws$u_up[s]        <- p$u_up
  draws$p_confirm[s]   <- p$p_confirm
  draws$fr_25_29[s]    <- p$fr["25-29"]
  draws$fr_30_34[s]    <- p$fr["30-34"]
  draws$fr_35_39[s]    <- p$fr["35-39"]
  draws$fr_40_44[s]    <- p$fr["40-44"]
  draws$fr_45_50[s]    <- p$fr["45-50"]

  # Run model for all age groups
  cost_fb_s <- cost_tl_s <- qaly_fb_s <- qaly_tl_s <- numeric(nrow(age_groups))

  for (i in 1:nrow(age_groups)) {
    ag  <- age_groups[i, ]
    fb  <- run_psa_arm("fembloc", ag, p)
    tl  <- run_psa_arm("tl",      ag, p)
    cost_fb_s[i] <- fb$cost
    cost_tl_s[i] <- tl$cost
    qaly_fb_s[i] <- fb$qaly
    qaly_tl_s[i] <- tl$qaly
  }

  # Weighted aggregate
  tc_fb <- sum(cost_fb_s * age_groups$prop)
  tc_tl <- sum(cost_tl_s * age_groups$prop)
  tq_fb <- sum(qaly_fb_s * age_groups$prop)
  tq_tl <- sum(qaly_tl_s * age_groups$prop)

  # NMB at each WTP
  for (w in seq_along(wtp_evppi)) {
    wtp <- wtp_evppi[w]
    nmb_fb_mat[s, w] <- wtp * tq_fb - tc_fb
    nmb_tl_mat[s, w] <- wtp * tq_tl - tc_tl
  }

  setTxtProgressBar(pb2, s)
}
close(pb2)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. EVPPI CALCULATION FUNCTION
# For each parameter group:
#   - Fit GAM: NMB_incremental ~ s(param1) + s(param2) + ...
#   - EVPPI = E[max(0, fitted_NMB)] - max(0, E[NMB])
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calc_evppi <- function(param_cols, wtp_vec,
                        nmb_fb, nmb_tl, draw_df) {

  inc_nmb <- nmb_fb - nmb_tl   # n_sim x n_wtp matrix

  evppi_vec <- numeric(length(wtp_vec))

  for (w in seq_along(wtp_vec)) {

    y <- inc_nmb[, w]

    # Build GAM formula dynamically
    if (length(param_cols) == 1) {
      gam_formula <- as.formula(paste("y ~ s(", param_cols, ")"))
    } else {
      smooth_terms <- paste0("s(", param_cols, ")", collapse = " + ")
      gam_formula  <- as.formula(paste("y ~", smooth_terms))
    }

    gam_data <- as.data.frame(draw_df[, param_cols, drop = FALSE])
    gam_data$y <- y

    # Fit GAM
    tryCatch({
      fit <- gam(gam_formula, data = gam_data)
      fitted_nmb <- fitted(fit)

      # EVPPI = E[max over strategies of fitted NMB] - max(E[NMB])
      # For 2 strategies: max(0, fitted_inc_NMB)
      evppi_vec[w] <- mean(pmax(0, fitted_nmb)) - max(0, mean(y))

    }, error = function(e) {
      evppi_vec[w] <<- NA
      warning(paste("GAM failed at WTP", wtp_vec[w], ":", e$message))
    })
  }

  evppi_vec
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CALCULATE EVPPI FOR EACH PARAMETER GROUP
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nCalculating EVPPI for 5 parameter groups...\n")

# EVPI (perfect info on all parameters) — upper bound
evpi_vec <- sapply(seq_along(wtp_evppi), function(w) {
  y <- nmb_fb_mat[, w] - nmb_tl_mat[, w]
  mean(pmax(0, y)) - max(0, mean(y))
})

cat("  Group 1: FemBloc fail rate...\n")
evppi_fail <- calc_evppi("p_fail_fb", wtp_evppi,
                          nmb_fb_mat, nmb_tl_mat, draws)

cat("  Group 2: FemBloc device cost...\n")
evppi_device <- calc_evppi("device_cost", wtp_evppi,
                            nmb_fb_mat, nmb_tl_mat, draws)

cat("  Group 3: Utility values (u_pc + u_up)...\n")
evppi_utility <- calc_evppi(c("u_pc", "u_up"), wtp_evppi,
                             nmb_fb_mat, nmb_tl_mat, draws)

cat("  Group 4: Confirmation rate...\n")
evppi_confirm <- calc_evppi("p_confirm", wtp_evppi,
                             nmb_fb_mat, nmb_tl_mat, draws)

cat("  Group 5: Fecundity ratios...\n")
evppi_fr <- calc_evppi(c("fr_25_29", "fr_30_34", "fr_35_39",
                          "fr_40_44", "fr_45_50"),
                        wtp_evppi, nmb_fb_mat, nmb_tl_mat, draws)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. SUMMARY TABLE AT KEY WTP THRESHOLDS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

key_wtp   <- c(100000, 200000, 300000, 500000)
key_idx   <- match(key_wtp, wtp_evppi)

evppi_summary <- data.frame(
  Parameter_Group   = c("EVPI (all parameters)",
                         "FemBloc fail rate",
                         "FemBloc device cost",
                         "Utility values",
                         "Confirmation rate",
                         "Fecundity ratios"),
  WTP_100k = round(c(evpi_vec[key_idx[1]],
                      evppi_fail[key_idx[1]],
                      evppi_device[key_idx[1]],
                      evppi_utility[key_idx[1]],
                      evppi_confirm[key_idx[1]],
                      evppi_fr[key_idx[1]])),
  WTP_200k = round(c(evpi_vec[key_idx[2]],
                      evppi_fail[key_idx[2]],
                      evppi_device[key_idx[2]],
                      evppi_utility[key_idx[2]],
                      evppi_confirm[key_idx[2]],
                      evppi_fr[key_idx[2]])),
  WTP_300k = round(c(evpi_vec[key_idx[3]],
                      evppi_fail[key_idx[3]],
                      evppi_device[key_idx[3]],
                      evppi_utility[key_idx[3]],
                      evppi_confirm[key_idx[3]],
                      evppi_fr[key_idx[3]])),
  WTP_500k = round(c(evpi_vec[key_idx[4]],
                      evppi_fail[key_idx[4]],
                      evppi_device[key_idx[4]],
                      evppi_utility[key_idx[4]],
                      evppi_confirm[key_idx[4]],
                      evppi_fr[key_idx[4]]))
)

cat("\n========== EVPPI SUMMARY (NOK per patient) ==========\n")
print(evppi_summary)

kable(evppi_summary,
      caption = "EVPPI by parameter group at key WTP thresholds (NOK per patient)",
      col.names = c("Parameter Group",
                    "NOK 100,000", "NOK 200,000",
                    "NOK 300,000", "NOK 500,000")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(1, bold = TRUE, background = "#f0f0f0")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. EVPPI CURVE PLOT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

evppi_long <- data.frame(
  wtp   = rep(wtp_evppi / 1000, 6),
  evppi = c(evpi_vec,
            evppi_fail,
            evppi_device,

                "FemBloc fail rate",

              each = length(wtp_evppi))
)

evppi_long$group <- factor(evppi_long$group,
  levels = c("EVPI (all parameters)",
             "FemBloc fail rate",

evppi_plot <- ggplot(evppi_long,
                     aes(x = wtp, y = evppi,
```
